rfm_tuples.R: Implied management commitment to balance-sheet repair and post-patent Rynaxypyr strategy following a 69.7% drawdown, $1.36B goodwill writedown, dividend cut to $0.08, and two consecutive covenant amendments.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — parse Form 4 XML for code-P (open-market purchases) by named directors/officers across the drawdown window (Oct 2025 to cutoff 2026-05-25).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three independent directors executed code-P open-market PURCHASES into the drawdown: (1) Director Michael F. Barry bought 18,072.191 shares on 2026-03-04 at $13.83 = $250,058 — five days after the FY25 10-K disclosed the $1.36B goodwill writedown, India $522M charges, the 86% dividend cut, and Amendment No. 5 to the credit facility; (2) Director John Mitchell Raines bought 7,000 shares on 2025-11-13 at $13.77 = $96,390 — about two weeks after the Q3'25 print and after the Oct 2025 dividend cut to $0.08; (3) Director Carol Anthony Davidson bought 10,000 shares on 2025-11-05 at $13.5957 = $135,957 — same window. Aggregate director open-market purchases since the dividend cut: ~$482,405 across three independent directors at prices $13.60-13.83. ZERO open-market purchases by CEO Brondeau, CFO Sandifer, or any C-suite officer. Insider sales in the same window: only code-F (tax withholding on vest) at $14.62 (2026-02-23) and $15.56 (2026-04-28). No code-S (discretionary sales) by officers since Scanlan EVP-HR $128K sale on 2025-09-29 at $34 — long before the worst news. Officer/director equity awards (code A) granted at fair value (FY25 PSU vesting and 2026 PSU grants Feb 19, 2026 priced at $14.62-15.56 — restricted to vest 2027-2029).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: MIXED but tilted POSITIVE — three independent directors stepped up with material personal cash ($250K, $136K, $96K) AT levels $13.60-13.83, post-cut, post-impairment, post-covenant-amendment. That is honest insider conviction. However, the ABSENCE of any code-P purchase by CEO Brondeau (68 years old, also Chairman) or any C-suite officer is the negative tell — the people closest to the operating reality have NOT put personal cash on the line. This pattern (directors yes, operators no) is the classic 'governance-aware capital allocation' signal, not the 'operators see undervaluation' signal that ABG and similar names show. Net: moderate positive, not a slam-dunk LONG tape.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: insider transactions timed independently of capital events / non-public information.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference Form 4 transaction dates against the 8-K calendar (capital events, earnings, divestitures, covenant amendments) for 2025-2026.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital event calendar: dividend reduced to $0.08 announced October 2025 (8-K 2025-10-29); Q3'25 earnings 8-K 2025-10-29; Subordinated Notes 8.45% 2055 issued May 27, 2025 ($750M); Amendment No. 5 to revolver (leverage cap → 6.00x) executed Dec 2025; FY25 10-K filed 2026-02-27 with $1.36B goodwill writedown disclosure; Amendment No. 6 to revolver (leverage testing suspended Q1-Q3 2026, cap → 6.75 thereafter, security/guarantors added) executed April 16, 2026 — disclosed in Q1'26 10-Q filed April 30, 2026. Davidson buy 2025-11-05 and Raines buy 2025-11-13 are 7-15 days AFTER the Q3 earnings 8-K (Oct 29) and the dividend-cut announcement — i.e., after material info was public, not before. Barry buy 2026-03-04 is 5 days after the FY25 10-K (Feb 27) — also after disclosure, not before. CRITICALLY: no insider sales of any kind in 30-day windows before either the Q3'25 print, the Q4'25/FY25 print, or the April 2026 Amendment No. 6. The only sales are code-F tax-withholding on PSU vests on 2026-02-23 (price $14.62), which are mechanical, not discretionary.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider timing is CLEAN. Buys post-bad-news, not pre. No clustered selling ahead of either covenant amendment, the dividend cut, or the goodwill writedown. This contradicts a 'liar' or 'pump-and-dump' pattern. The drawdown looks like genuine business deterioration disclosed honestly, not concealed.

rfm_tuples.R: "We recorded a $1,356.2 million write-off of our remaining goodwill balance in connection with the impairment test." (Item 7 + Note 4)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the writedown was fully recognized; Mode B — assess whether the remaining-goodwill phrasing signals zero residual cushion for future impairment.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 7 + Note 4 + cash flow recon)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: $1,356.2M goodwill writedown taken in Q4 2025 — 100% of remaining goodwill. Combined with $522M India held-for-sale write-down and $271.5M restructuring charges, total non-cash charges = ~$2.15B in 2025. Net loss attributable to stockholders $2,238.9M (vs net income $341.1M in FY24). Adjusted EBITDA $842.7M (down 7%) — implies pre-impairment business is still cash-generative. Revenue $3,467.4M down 18% (down 8% ex-India). Cash $584.5M at YE25 (up from $357.3M YE24) but $577.3M is foreign-subsidiary cash, requiring repatriation planning. The writedown size relative to enterprise value at cutoff is enormous (~50% of pre-drawdown market cap).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honesty signal is clean — the writedown is FULL and final (no remaining goodwill to be impaired later). But the magnitude and the disclosure that the trigger was 'significant decrease in our stock price during the fourth quarter' means the auditor forced the writedown after the market repriced — i.e., management did NOT proactively recognize the impairment, the market did. The business itself is severely impaired: Rynaxypyr (formerly the moat) is now post-patent, India business is being sold at writedown values, and management's response (Project Foundation + Project Focus) is yielding only $165M in cost benefits against $2B+ in charges.

rfm_tuples.R: "In December 2025, the Company amended its credit agreement to provide additional financial flexibility given current market challenges." (Note 12, FY25 10-K)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given Amendment No. 5 in Dec 2025, look for evidence of further amendments needed before cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Amendment No. 5 (Dec 2025): max leverage ratio raised to 6.00x through Sep 30, 2026, stepping down to 3.75x by Q4 2028; min interest coverage lowered to 2.00x through Jun 30, 2027. Dividend increase restrictions added. FOUR MONTHS LATER, Amendment No. 6 (April 16, 2026, disclosed in Q1'26 10-Q): leverage ratio test SUSPENDED for Q1-Q3 2026, then capped at 6.75x through Dec 2027, stepping down to 3.75x by Q1 2029. Min interest coverage lowered to 2.00x through Jun 30, 2027 stepping to 3.50x by Q1 2029. CRITICALLY, the April 2026 Amendment also added subsidiary guarantors and granted security interests — i.e., the revolver went from unsecured to SECURED. This is a meaningful credit-quality step down.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: TWO covenant amendments in four months, with the second one MORE LENIENT than the first and also requiring SECURITY/GUARANTORS, signals the Dec 2025 amendment was inadequate. The company had to come back to lenders within one quarter and ask for: (a) complete suspension of leverage testing for three quarters, (b) a higher long-run cap (6.75x vs 6.00x), and (c) collateral. This is the strongest single Mode-B catch — the issuer's Dec 2025 narrative implied 'we have addressed this', but Q1'26 reality required another, more invasive amendment. RED-FLAG_NEGATIVE-adjacent. Combined with the $586M of 2026 debt maturities (per FY25 10-K maturity table — $1.4 and $1.6 unamortized + $586M maturing within one year), the balance-sheet pressure is real and accelerating.

rfm_tuples.R: "In light of the challenges that the company is facing and to further prioritize debt reduction, the Board of Directors in October 2025 made the decision to reduce the quarterly dividend to $0.08 per share." (FY25 10-K)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the magnitude and prior level; Mode B — assess whether the cut was sized to reflect distress.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Prior quarterly dividend was $0.58/share (since 2024); reduced to $0.08/share starting January 2026 — a 86% cut. Annualized savings ~$250M ($2.00/share x ~125M sh outstanding). January 2026 dividend payment totaled $10.0M (vs ~$72.5M at the prior rate). This dividend was uninterrupted since 2006. Combined with the new credit-agreement restriction on dividend increases (Amendment No. 5), this is effectively a deep cut with no near-term path to restoration.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is honest and proportionate, but the SEVERITY of the cut (86%) — bigger than the typical 50% "signaling cut" — implies management/board see this as a multi-year balance-sheet problem, not a one-year cyclical dip. The fact that the cut was decided in October 2025 (before the goodwill writedown was even taken) suggests management was already braced for the worst. Consistent with the covenant-amendment pattern: management is in defensive mode. Note: a dividend cut combined with covenant relief combined with insider PURCHASES (directors only) is the classic 'kitchen-sink reset' setup, which historically has positive forward returns IF the underlying business stabilizes.

rfm_tuples.R: "Our 2026 operational priorities... include... managing our post-patent Rynaxypyr active strategy." (FY25 10-K) and "lower pricing to diamide partners, pricing actions on branded Rynaxypyr active" (Q1'26 10-Q).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify that Rynaxypyr generic competition is now reflected in price and volume; check whether the pricing actions are voluntary or forced.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Rynaxypyr (chlorantraniliprole) was FMC's largest single product, ~$1.5B+ revenue at peak — protected by composition-of-matter patents that began expiring 2022-2026 across jurisdictions. FY25 10-K language is reactive ("managing" post-patent) rather than offensive. Q1'26 10-Q confirms: revenue down 4% YoY to $758.6M driven by "lower pricing to diamide partners" (i.e., FMC sells active to licensees Syngenta, Sumitomo, ISK at lower prices because generics are now in market) AND "pricing actions on branded Rynaxypyr active" (i.e., FMC is cutting its own branded price to defend share). Volume was actually up YoY in EMEA/NA — i.e., the issue is PRICE, not VOLUME, which is the diagnostic of generic entry. Mode B catch: management does NOT quantify what % of revenue is now post-patent vs still-protected, nor what the run-rate Rynaxypyr revenue is post-generic.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The structural issue is acknowledged but under-quantified. Investors cannot model post-patent ARR for the largest molecule without disclosure of (a) jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction patent expiry, (b) generic share already taken, (c) license-fee step-down from Syngenta/Sumitomo. This is a Mode-B disclosure gap that matters more than the 10-K admits, but it is consistent with industry norm (Corteva and Bayer also obscure their molecule-level exposure). New active ingredients in the pipeline (Isoflex, fluindapyr, Dodhylex, rimisoxafen) are mentioned but not quantified.

rfm_tuples.R: "In July 2025, the Board of Directors approved a plan to divest the Company's commercial business in India... The sale process is underway and is expected to conclude in 2026." (FY25 10-K)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the divestiture is being executed; Mode B — assess whether the write-down values imply a forced sale.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Held-for-sale accounting triggered Q3 2025. $522M of one-time charges and write-downs taken in 2025 to position the India business for sale, including $521.7M classified under 'India held for sale business' in the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation. Q1'26 10-Q: sale process still ongoing, no buyer announced as of filing date 2026-04-30. The company plans to retain a supply agreement post-sale (i.e., keep manufacturing in India, sell only the commercial/distribution business). 10-K says India was ~10% of revenue in 2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is honest about the size of write-downs but does NOT quantify the expected sale proceeds or net cash impact. A 10-month sale process with no buyer announced (as of cutoff) for an emerging-market commercial business written down by $500M+ is consistent with a difficult, possibly distressed sale. Mode B gap: management does not disclose the bid range or buyer universe. Material because the proceeds are earmarked for debt paydown — a delayed/lower sale undermines the deleveraging narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: "Revenue of $758.6 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 decreased $32.8 million, or approximately 4 percent." (Q1'26 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check whether Q1'26 results confirm or contradict the FY25 10-K's '2026 priorities' framing of stabilization.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1'26: revenue $758.6M (-4% YoY), net loss attributable $281.3M (vs net loss $15.5M Q1'25) = a $265.8M deterioration. Increase driven by $112.1M tax-valuation-allowance charge (Switzerland) + $59.2M increase in restructuring/other charges. Underlying operating performance is masked by these items, but the trajectory is negative. Q1 is seasonally the largest quarter for FMC (NH spring application season) so a 4% decline + tax charges + restructuring is a poor leading indicator.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Q1'26 does NOT confirm the '2026 stabilization' framing from the 10-K. Revenue is still declining, and the company is taking more restructuring charges plus a non-cash but signaling tax-valuation-allowance increase (a Swiss valuation allowance typically signals doubt about future taxable profits in that jurisdiction — a forward-looking negative). The April Amendment No. 6 was likely triggered by Q1 deterioration.

rfm_tuples.R: CEO Pierre R. Brondeau (age 68) listed as "Chief Executive Officer (24-present, 10-20); Chairman of the Board (10-present); Executive Chairman of the Board (20-21)" — i.e., he was re-instated as CEO in 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the 'CEO transition' restructuring charges in 2024 and the back-to-back distress signals, assess governance posture.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (FY25 10-K executive officer section + restructuring note)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mark Douglas was the prior CEO; Brondeau returned as CEO in 2024 (after serving as CEO 2010-2020, then Executive Chairman 2020-21). 2024 restructuring includes "$55.8 million in severance and employee separation charges, including costs associated with the CEO transition." Brondeau is now 68 years old and combines CEO + Chairman roles. The FY25 10-K does NOT disclose a succession plan, search process, or named president/COO successor. Q1'26 10-Q confirms Brondeau still in role. CFO Andrew Sandifer is also relatively long-tenured.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B disclosure gap: a 68-year-old founder-style CEO recalled to fix the business, no named successor, and a combined Chairman+CEO role at a company in covenant distress is a governance concern. Not fraud — but limits the pipeline of forward credibility if Brondeau's recovery plan does not deliver in 2026. The director buys ($482K aggregate) without ANY CEO/CFO open-market buying suggests even the board is hedging — endorsing the company but not yet endorsing the operating team's confidence.

rfm_tuples.R: FY25 10-K Item 3 (Legal Proceedings) and patent enforcement discussions in Item 1.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — confirm no material pending litigation that could accelerate balance-sheet pressure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: No new material litigation disclosed. Patent enforcement against generic Rynaxypyr producers in China and India is ongoing but not quantified as a contingent liability. Standard environmental remediation accruals continue. No going-concern qualification from auditors. No 13D activist filing visible in EDGAR filings before cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Litigation/legal posture is normal-course. No accelerator on the downside.

supplemental_signals.leverage_cap_progression: Pre: 3.75x baseline -> Amendment 5 (Dec 2025): 6.00x peak -> Amendment 6 (Apr 2026): leverage TEST SUSPENDED Q1-Q3 2026, then 6.75x cap; revolver moved from unsecured to SECURED with subsidiary guarantors

summary: FMC presents a mixed honesty-alpha profile. Strong POSITIVE signals: (1) three independent directors made open-market PURCHASES totaling ~$482K at $13.60-13.83 post-dividend-cut and post-10-K, with Director Michael F. Barry's $250K buy five days after the FY25 10-K being the strongest single Form-4 tell; (2) clean insider-timing (all buys are post-disclosure, zero pre-disclosure selling, only mechanical code-F vest withholdings); (3) honest, comprehensive disclosure of the $1.36B goodwill writedown, India $522M held-for-sale charges, and the 86% dividend cut. NEGATIVE signals (Mode B catches): (1) TWO covenant amendments in four months with the second one suspending leverage testing entirely Q1-Q3 2026 AND moving revolver to secured — the strongest single bear signal; (2) Q1'26 deterioration (revenue -4%, net loss -$281M) contradicts the FY25 10-K's stabilization narrative; (3) Rynaxypyr post-patent transition under-quantified; (4) absent CEO/CFO personal buying despite director conviction. Verdict: LONG-tier (honesty-alpha framework rewards transparent distress with insider buy-side validation), but smaller position size than ABG due to (a) escalating covenant pressure, (b) no operator-level insider buying, and (c) Q1'26 trajectory.
